newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-May 29.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-May 29.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday:
** India's largest steelmaker SAIL says its net profit plunges to 5.27 billion rupees for the year ended March 31, from 13.19 billion in the previous year
** Multinational firm Colgate-Palmolive (India) says its 1996/97 net rises marginally to 780.3 million rupees, from 775.8 million in the previous year
** Telecommunications firm Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd says its net surges to 8.87 billion rupees, from 7.3 billion in 1995/96
** Refiner Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd announces a net profit of 4.33 billion rupees, up from 3.86 billion in the previous year
** Earnings are due from Larsen & Toubro later today and from electrical engineering firm Siemens on Friday

** Textiles machinery firm Lakshmi Machine Works says its 1996/97 net falls to 237.8 million rupees, from 429.6 million in the previous year. But the firm says it will offer its shareholders one bonus share for every one held
** India's tobacco and hotel conglomerate ITC Ltd will invest eight billion rupees in cigarette manufacturing and modernisation of its units over the next five years, company officials say

The company which posted a net profit of 3.4 billion rupees in 1996/97 compared with 2.6 billion a year earlier will focus on its core competent areas -- tobacco, hotels, speciality papers and packaging, officials say

** State-run Corporation Bank plans its maiden public issue of equity shares in end August to raise 2.66 billion rupees, an official says. The bank plans to offer 38 million shares. Each 10 rupee face value share would be priced at around 70 rupees, he adds
** State-owned telephone monopoly MTNL should tap overseas markets based on its 1996/97 results, analysts say
Analysts predict a 25 percent increase in the company's 1997/98 net profit
But they express concerns over MTNL's falling revenue per line, the government's reluctance to hike domestic tariffs, and the surge in its 1996/97 net profit following a drop in its tax payout
** Bombay's benchmark stocks index .BSESN closes 7.25 points, or 0.20 percent, lower at 3685.31 on Wednesday as results of Colgate and SAIL disappoint market
